notes: §1985:VII.3.6.3 GR2: "STANDARD specifies that labels exist for the file or the device to which the file is assigned and the labels conform to the implementor's label specifications." The rule leaves the labels to the implementor. The implementation's label specification is that a file carries no label record the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (§1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program."), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states the clause as accepted-inert at 85. So STANDARD asks nothing of the data the program transfers, and the code does nothing with it: labelRecordsClause parses the clause, its FileDescriptionFormats.Rows row admits it in every file description format, VisitLabelRecordsClause is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, refused from 2002), and BindFileSection has no arm for it, so no connector reads or writes a label. Probed at 85: LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD and LABEL RECORD STANDARD compile, and the file written is byte for byte the file the same program writes under OMITTED or with no clause. The witness writes one record to a file described LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD and reads it back. The grammar also takes words other than STANDARD and OMITTED; that is the general format's row and kb/Work PB5070, not this rule.
